title: Mass on a spring

subjects.description: small green rectangular block hanging from a vertical spring

observation.what_happens: A green block hangs from a vertical spring under a fixed support and bobs up and down. The oscillation continues through the whole clip, starting near equilibrium and still oscillating at the end.

calibration.note: no scale: lengths are in pixels

reasoning: The track is straight with period about 0.7 s and peaks falling from 124 to 89 px while troughs rise from 0 to 46 px, so motion is a vertical spring oscillation decaying toward equilibrium near 65 px. This suggests a harmonic restoring force plus light damping in air. Candidates compare ideal, linear viscous damped, and linear plus quadratic air-drag models.

critique.finding: The block bobs as a damped spring swinging at {omega} around {s_eq} with damping {gamma}, kept alive by a push of size {F_drive} at frequency {w_drive}. It only partly captures the motion, leaving a regular wiggle in its misses.
critique.headline: Driven spring keeps bobbing near resonance
critique.revision_idea: Add cubic spring stiffness to let frequency shift with amplitude. The remaining misses still swing up and down in step with the bobbing instead of scattering like noise.
critique.why_it_won: It keeps oscillating through the whole clip with a periodic push while plain damped or ideal springs fade or swing far from the measured track.

preRevision.revision_idea: Add a gentle periodic push from the support near the bobbing rate. The misses swing with the motion and persist to the end instead of fading, which a sustained push would explain.

postRevision.revision_idea: Add cubic spring stiffness to let frequency shift with amplitude. The remaining misses still swing up and down in step with the bobbing instead of scattering like noise.

headline: Driven spring keeps bobbing near resonance
finding: The block bobs as a damped spring swinging at about 9.1 rad/s around about 67 px with damping about 1.5 1/s, kept alive by a push of size about 343 px/s² at frequency about 8.5 rad/s. It only partly captures the motion, leaving a regular wiggle in its misses.

eyeball.confidence: low - single static frame provided, timing of oscillation inferred from typical demo
eyeball.law_in_words: vertical mass on spring is damped harmonic oscillator about gravity-shifted equilibrium: x_double_dot + gamma * x_dot + omega^2 * (x - s_eq) = 0, with omega = sqrt(k/m)

clockCheck.why: Clock not checked: with no ruler in view and no length stated, gravity can’t be measured in metres. A slowed clip would look the same.
